consensus_summary: The responses recognize two leading senses of “seed”: the word or gospel sown in human hearts, and promised offspring culminating in Christ. All explicitly recognize the word-of-God sense, with several treating it as primary in the parable of the sower.
book_summary: Seed signifies the word of God sown in human hearts.
consensus_core_identification: The word or message of God sown in human hearts.
book_core_identification: The word of God sown in human hearts.
boundary_disagreement: None within the cited parable context. The consensus additionally recognizes other context-dependent meanings of “seed,” but the book entry does not explicitly deny them.
material_contradiction: None. The book states one of the consensus’s dominant and explicitly scriptural identifications.
rationale: After reducing both readings to their minimum core, they identify the same referent: God’s word as seed received in human hearts. Differences in wording are immaterial, and the consensus’s catalog of other biblical uses does not conflict with this glossary entry unless the entry is taken as an exclusive definition for every occurrence.
strongest_objection: The consensus is divided over whether this is the single primary meaning, since messianic offspring is also prominent and “seed” is context-dependent. Nevertheless, Luke 8:11 directly and exactly supports the book’s identification in its cited context.
